column1: # Where the fish that are NOT in the agreed OrthoFinder tree go in the master species tree (config/species_tree_master.nwk).
# Read by `cichlid_data.master_tree.build()`; one row per fish, applied in the order of this file (an anchor may be a fish placed earlier).
# A fish with no row falls back to the older rule: next to its TreeFam relative, or as a child of its ladder level's clade.
# The agreed tree is never changed: pruned to its 35 species the master equals it (checked).
# op:      sister_of    new node (anchor, species) in the place of the anchor clade; `group` optionally names the new node
#          join_group   the species joins the group node `group`; the first member creates it in the place of the anchor clade,
#                       with the anchor inside it, so the group is (anchor, member, member, ...), an unresolved polytomy
#          group_under  the species joins the group node `group`; the first member creates it as an extra child of the anchor
#          child_of     the species is an extra child of the anchor node (a polytomy there)
# anchor:  species (comma-separated: their last common ancestor), or @Teleostei, @Percomorpha, @Ovalentaria, @Cichlidae
# support: robust       the placement is supported by the published work cited
#          contested    published phylogenies disagree, so the relationships are deliberately left unresolved (a polytomy)
#          by_default   the sources used do not resolve it; left unresolved
# A relationship that is in doubt is NEVER resolved to make the tree look tidier: an invented resolution would make
# a speciation look like a duplication, or the reverse, in the homology decider.
# Family and order membership below is from the classification of Betancur-R et al. 2017 (BMC Evol Biol 17:162,
# doi 10.1186/s12862-017-0958-3); membership marked "to confirm" is standard taxonomy that was not read in the paper itself.
